extracted.intended_audience: users of Plural (Singular) working with the non-commutative subsystem (mathematicians / computer-algebra users / developers)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for the Plural non-commutative subsystem: types (ideal, map, module, poly, qring, resolution, ring) and functions (betti, bracket, dim, division, eliminate, envelope, fetch, etc.), with syntax, semantics, notes and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: ideal expression
rubrics_metrics.description: An ideal expression is: 1. an identifier of type ideal; 2. a function returning an ideal; 3. a combination of ideal expressions by the arithmetic operations + or *; 4. a power of an ideal expression (operator ^ or **); 5. a type cast to ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: i*i involves all products of generators of i while i^2 involves only the different ones and is therefore faster. Examples show construction from vectors/polynomials, type-casting, and using maxideal. See also simplification (Section 5.1.139).

rubrics_metrics.name: ideal operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Operations defined on ideal expressions: + (addition = concatenation of the generators and simplification), * (multiplication with ideal, poly, vector, module; result simplified when multiplied with ideal or module), ^ (exponentiation by a non-negative integer), and indexing ideal_expression[intvec_expression] to access polynomial generators (index 1 gives first generator).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiplication semantics: I*J computes all products of generators; I^n may be faster. Examples illustrate simplification effects (I+0, I*x, I*J), multiplication with vectors, and m^2 listing monomials. See simplification notes and Section 5.1.139.

rubrics_metrics.name: ideal related functions (plural)
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions related to ideals: dim, eliminate, intersect, kbase, lead, lift, liftstd, maxideal, modulo, mres, ncols, nres, oppose, preimage, quotient, reduce, simplify, size, slimgb, std, subst, syz, twostd, vdim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short meanings given inline: dim = Gelfand-Kirillov dimension of basering modulo leading ideal; eliminate = elimination of variables; intersect = ideal intersection; kbase = vector space basis of basering modulo leading ideal; lead = leading terms; lift/liftstd = lift-matrix / left Groebner basis+transformation matrix; maxideal = generators of power of maximal ideal at 0; modulo = represents quotient relation; mres/nres = minimal/free resolutions; ncols = number of columns; oppose = create opposite ideal; preimage/quotient/reduce/simplify/size/std/slimgb/subst/syz/twostd/vdim described in cross-references. See referenced sections for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: map (plural)
rubrics_metrics.description: Maps are ring maps from a preimage ring (source) into the basering (target), defined by specifying images for source variables in the target ring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: target is ALWAYS the actual basering; preimage ring must be stored by name so maps can only be used where preimage name can be resolved. Canonical/coercion mappings between coefficient fields are listed (Q→Q(a,..), Q→R, Q→C, Z/p→(Z/p)(a,..), Z/p→GF(pn), Z/p→R, R→C); additionally Q→Z/p etc. Warning: when mapping Q→Z/p distribute numerator and denominator via Z→Z/p so numbers with denominators divisible by the characteristic are not allowed. Recommendation: map only objects with integer coefficients in such cases. In non-commutative case maps may fail to be morphisms. Examples show M(P), F(P) returning kernel behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: map declarations (plural)
rubrics_metrics.description: Syntax forms: map name = preimage ring name, ideal expression; map name = preimage ring name, list of poly and ideal expressions; map name = map expression;. Purpose: defines a ring map from preimage_ring to basering by mapping variables of preimage to generators of the ideal (excess or missing elements handled as specified). Default: none.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If ideal contains fewer elements than number of variables, remaining variables map to 0; extra elements are ignored. The image ring is always the current basering. There are standard mappings fetch and imap. The name of a map serves as a function mapping objects from preimage ring into basering; preimage objects must be defined by names (no evaluation in preimage ring). Examples illustrate non-morphism behavior and mapping central elements to zero.

rubrics_metrics.name: map expression
rubrics_metrics.description: A map expression is: 1. an identifier of type map; 2. a function returning map; 3. a composition of maps using parentheses, e.g. f(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: map expression[int_expressions] indexes the image of the corresponding variable. Composition f(g) yields f∘g when target of g is basering of f. Examples show involutive endomorphism and composition yielding identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: map operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Operations: ( ) composition of maps; map_expression[int_expressions] returns a map entry (image of variable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Composition only valid when target rings line up. Example: F; G=F(F); G yields swapped images and G(p)==p checks identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: map related functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Related helper functions: fetch (identity map between rings and qrings), imap (convenient map procedure for inclusions and projections), preimage (preimage under a ring map), subst (substitute a ring variable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References: see specific sections for implementation details. fetch/imap facilitate maps close to identity or inclusions/projections; preimage and subst are used in ring-mapping workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: module (plural)
rubrics_metrics.description: Modules are left submodules of a free module over the basering with basis gen(1), gen(2), ..., represented by lists of vectors which generate the left submodule. Finitely generated R-modules are represented by their module of relations (Coker-representation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignments module M=v1,...,vk; matrix A=M create the presentation matrix of size n×k with columns the generators. Generators may be viewed as relations of R^n / M. Examples show building modules from vectors and printing matrix format.

rubrics_metrics.name: module declarations (plural)
rubrics_metrics.description: Syntax: module name = list of vector expressions; or module name = module expression;. Purpose: defines a left module. Default: [0].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example constructs module from vectors and demonstrates print(m) showing columns generating m. See examples in U(so_3) context.

rubrics_metrics.name: module expressions
rubrics_metrics.description: A module expression is: 1. an identifier of type module; 2. a function returning module; 3. module expressions combined by +; 4. multiplication of a module expression with an ideal or a poly expression: *; 5. a type cast to module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indexing forms module_expression[int_expression,int_expression] for module entry (row,column) and module_expressions[int_expression] for a column vector. Example shows combining modules and matrix conversions.

rubrics_metrics.name: module operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Module operations: + addition (concatenation of generators and simplification); multiplication (right or left) with number, ideal, or poly (but not 'module * module'); indexing forms to access entries or vectors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: '-' implicitly converts a module into a matrix in examples. Multiplication with ideal/poly produces left/right multiplied generators. Examples show matrix subtraction and printing results.

rubrics_metrics.name: module related functions (plural)
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions related to modules: eliminate, freemodule, intersect, kbase, lead, lift, liftstd, modulo, mres, ncols, nres, nrows, oppose, print, prune, quotient, reduce, simplify, size, std, subst, syz, vdim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short meanings: freemodule = free module of given rank; intersect = module intersection; kbase = vector space basis of free module modulo leading module; lift/liftstd = lift-matrix / left Groebner basis + transformation matrix; mres/nres = compute minimal/free resolutions; prune = minimize embedding into free module; reduce = left normal form w.r.t left Groebner basis; syz = first syzygy module; vdim = vector space dimension mod leading terms. See cross-references for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: poly (plural)
rubrics_metrics.description: Polynomials and vectors are basic data: polynomials consist of finitely many terms (coefficient*monomial) combined by usual operations. Polynomials can only be defined or accessed with respect to a basering determining coefficient type, indeterminant names, and monomial ordering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remark: conventions on polynomial multiplication are given (see Section 7.1). Examples show defining ring and polynomials including indexed exponents and short/long print forms; short=0 toggles display.

rubrics_metrics.name: poly declarations (plural)
rubrics_metrics.description: Syntax: poly name = poly expression ; Purpose: defines a polynomial. Default: 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show declaration in differential-like operator rings and non-commutative relations; polynomials with parameters and integer-indexed exponents are illustrated.

rubrics_metrics.name: poly expressions
rubrics_metrics.description: A polynomial expression is (optional parts in square brackets): 1. a monomial ([coefficient] ring_variable [exponent] [ring_variable [exponent] ...]) (NO spaces allowed inside a monomial); 2. an identifier of type poly; 3. a function returning poly; 4. polynomial expressions combined by +,-,*,/,^; 5. a type cast to poly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monomials containing an indexed ring variable must be built from ring_variable and coefficient with operations * and ^. Examples show Weyl algebra instances, lead()/leadmonom(), simplify(), cleardenom() behaviors and normalization of leading coefficients.

rubrics_metrics.name: poly operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Operations on polys: + addition, - negation/subtraction, * multiplication, / commutative division by a monomial (non-divisible terms yield 0), ^/** power by a positive integer, comparisons (<,<=,>,>=,==,<>) compare leading monomials, and poly_expression[intvec_expression] returns sum of monomials at indicated places w.r.t ordering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these operations respecting monomial ordering. Examples illustrate leading monomial comparisons and normalize/cleardenom for denominators.

rubrics_metrics.name: poly related functions (plural)
rubrics_metrics.description: Related functions: bracket (Lie bracket), lead (leading term), leadcoef (coefficient of leading term), leadexp (exponent vector of leading monomial), leadmonom (leading monomial), oppose, reduce (left normal form), simplify, size, subst, var.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brief behaviors: bracket computes pq-qp with Leibniz rule; reduce gives left normal form wrt left Groebner basis; simplify normalizes polynomial; size = number of monomials; subst substitutes ring variables; oppose creates opposite polynomial into a basering. Cross-references to sections provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: qring (plural)
rubrics_metrics.description: qring: compute within factor-rings modulo two-sided ideals. The ideal must be given as a two-sided Groebner basis (twostd command).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation: turn on option(redSB); option(redTail); when computing in qrings to avoid difficult interpretations. See Section 3.3 for rings and quotient rings.

rubrics_metrics.name: qring declaration (plural)
rubrics_metrics.description: Syntax: qring name = ideal expression ; Purpose: declares a quotient ring as the basering modulo an ideal_expression and sets it as current basering. Default: none.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: reports error if an ideal is not a two-sided Groebner basis. Example shows error message and using twostd(i) to create a valid qring; then use reduce(std(0)) to get reduced forms in quotient. Non-commutative relations among variables are shown in examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: qring related functions (plural)
rubrics_metrics.description: Related functions: envelope (enveloping ring), nvars (number of ring variables), opposite (opposite ring), setring (set a new basering).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These functions assist in working with quotient rings and switching baserings. See referenced sections for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: resolution (plural)
rubrics_metrics.description: The type resolution is an intermediate representation retaining additional information from computation of resolutions; enables use of partial results to compute Betti numbers or minimal resolutions. Resolutions defined only w.r.t. a basering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: to access elements of a resolution assign it to a list (this completes computations and may take time). Direct access with brackets causes implicit cast to a list.

rubrics_metrics.name: resolution declarations (plural)
rubrics_metrics.description: Syntax: resolution name = resolution expression ; Purpose: defines a resolution. Default: none.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example constructs resolution re=nres(i,0), shows printout that resolution is not minimized yet, conversion to list to inspect matrices, and checks product of matrices is zero.

rubrics_metrics.name: resolution expressions (plural)
rubrics_metrics.description: A resolution expression is: 1. an identifier of type resolution; 2. a function returning a resolution; 3. a type cast to resolution from a list of ideals or modules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resolutions can be produced by nres/mres and cast from lists to access internal matrices (syzygies, differentials).

rubrics_metrics.name: resolution related functions (plural)
rubrics_metrics.description: Related functions: betti (Betti numbers), minres (minimizes a free resolution), mres, nres (compute resolutions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: betti computes graded Betti numbers from a minimal resolution; minres reduces a resolution; mres/nres produce minimal/full resolutions. See detailed betti entry for matrix interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: ring (plural)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rings describe properties of polynomials, ideals, etc. Almost all computations in Plural require a basering. Rings include coefficient field, variable names, and monomial ordering. Non-commutative structures over commutative rings are constructed via nc_algebra.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plural usually works with global orderings but some local orderings allowed in graded commutative rings. Basering selection strongly affects behavior of polynomials/ideals/modules. See Section 3.3 for detailed concept.

rubrics_metrics.name: ring declarations (plural)
rubrics_metrics.description: Syntax: ring name = (coefficient field), (names of ring variables), (ordering); Default: 32003,(x,y,z),(dp,C); Purpose: declares a ring and sets it as the actual basering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coefficient field options: non-negative int ≤2147483647; list of int expression and names; 'real'; 'complex' with options. Names must be list of names or indexed names. Ordering is list of block orderings: lp/dp/Dp optionally with size; wp/Wp/a with weight vector; M(intmat); c or C. If one component has single entry parentheses may be omitted. Examples show composing rings and tensor products using nc_algebra and setring.

rubrics_metrics.name: ring operations
rubrics_metrics.description: + constructs a tensor product C = A ⊗K B of two G-algebras A and B over the ground field, with relations combining those of A and B and commuting relations between x_i and y_j.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidelines for ground fields k1,k2 for A⊗K B: neither may be R or C; if characteristics differ one must be Q; at most one may have parameters; if one is algebraic extension of Z/p it may not be defined by charstr of type (p^n,a). Use ring(list) or ringlist to decompose/compose rings. Examples show building U(sl_2) + Weyl algebra and combining orderings/blocks.

rubrics_metrics.name: ring related functions (plural)
rubrics_metrics.description: Related functions: charstr (description of coefficient field), envelope, npars (number of ring parameters), nvars (number of ring variables), opposite (opposite ring), ordstr (monomial ordering), parstr (names of ring parameters), qring (quotient ring), ringlist (decompose ring), setring (set new basering), varstr (names of ring variables).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These helpers inspect and manipulate ring metadata (ordering, variables, parameters) and produce derived rings (envelope, opposite). See cross-referenced sections for usage and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: functions chapter: general syntax
rubrics_metrics.description: General syntax of a function: [target =] function name(<arguments>); Control structures and system variables of Plural are same as Singular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This chapter (7.3) is a complete reference of built-in Plural kernel commands; library functions are in Section 7.7. Users should follow the function signatures and types given in each function's entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: betti (plural)
rubrics_metrics.description: Syntax: betti(list expression) | betti(resolution expression) | betti(..., int expression). Type: intmat. Purpose: with 1 argument computes graded Betti numbers of a minimal resolution of R^n / M if R has homogeneous relations and the argument is a resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Output intmat entry d at (i,j) is minimal number of generators in degree i+j of the j-th syzygy module. betti uses only initial monomials so non-homogeneous input may give confusing results. Optional second argument non-zero will minimize Betti numbers. Printable with print( , 'betti'). Example demonstrates computing Betti numbers from mres and printing formatted output.

rubrics_metrics.name: bracket
rubrics_metrics.description: Syntax: bracket(poly expression, poly expression). Type: poly. Purpose: computes the Lie bracket [p,q]=pq-qp of first polynomial with second; uses special routines based on the Leibniz rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: using a quantum-deformed U(so_3), bracket(p,q) returns 0 if p is central. Other examples show common non-zero brackets. Useful for Lie-like computations in non-commutative rings.

rubrics_metrics.name: dim (plural)
rubrics_metrics.description: Syntax: dim(ideal expression) | dim(module expression). Type: int. Computes the Gelfand-Kirillov dimension of the ideal/module generated by leading monomials of the given generators (dimension of ideal/submodule if represented by a left Groebner basis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For a submodule of a free module, dimension is GK-dimension of left module with given presentation. Computed GK-dimension is relative to ground field; to get complete GK-dimension add transcendence degree of ground field. Examples show dim(std(0)) for ring and dim(std(I)) for module.

rubrics_metrics.name: division (plural)
rubrics_metrics.description: Syntax: division(ideal expression, ideal expression [, int expression [, intvec expression]]) or module variants. Type: list. Purpose: computes a left division with remainder returning list T,R,U where T is matrix, R left ideal/module (remainder), U diagonal matrix of units satisfying transpose(U)*transpose(matrix(M)) = transpose(T)*transpose(matrix(N)) + transpose(matrix(R)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: division uses different algorithms depending on whether N is represented by a Groebner basis. For GR-algebras U is identity. Optional third/fourth arguments bound weighted degree and weight vector. Example shows division producing cofactors and remainder and verifying identity via matrix equation. See lift for computing T as well.

rubrics_metrics.name: eliminate (plural)
rubrics_metrics.description: Syntax: eliminate(ideal expression, product of ring variables) or eliminate(module expression, product of ring variables). Type: same as first argument. Purpose: eliminates variables occurring as factors of second argument from an ideal/module by intersecting with subring not containing these variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: eliminate does not need special ordering nor a Groebner basis and does not work in non-commutative quotients. In non-commutative algebras, not every subset of variables generates a proper subalgebra; elimination may fail with error 'no elimination is possible: subalgebra is not admissible'. Examples show eliminating parameter 'a' succeeds, while trying to eliminate 'h' fails because subalgebra generated by e,f is not closed.

rubrics_metrics.name: envelope
rubrics_metrics.description: Syntax: envelope(ring name). Type: ring. Purpose: creates an enveloping algebra Aenv = A ⊗_K Aopp, where Aopp is the opposite algebra of A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must activate the ring with setring to use the enveloping algebra. Presentation of Aenv follows from opposite; examples show constructing Aenv for U(sl_2), setting new basering and inspecting variables and block orderings. See oppose/opposite sections for related commands.

rubrics_metrics.name: fetch (plural)
rubrics_metrics.description: Syntax: fetch(ring name, name). Type: (identity map related). Purpose: the identity map between rings and qrings (used as standard mapping close to identity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referenced as a standard mapping for maps close to the identity. See map related functions and Section 7.3.7 for details.
